assumptions.description: Task-defined equal analytical allocation: 375 rows in each sex x age band, with integer age uniform within the band. This is not a Mexican population age distribution; source age and sex composition never determine these quotas.

All fictional rows represent the complete task eligibility statement. Unrepresented diagnosis, fasting-hour, measurement-route, pregnancy/lactation and availability fields are not simulated or verified. No medication or anemia exclusion is inferred.

Transport the Jansen BMI mean/SD and glucose and HbA1c reference intercepts/residual scales provisionally to eligible Mexico adults. Source European ancestry/GWAS-family selection, older composition, anemia exclusion, fasting duration and assay differences remain unresolved. These anchors are not estimates of target moments.

Use the fixed 18.0 glucose conversion and published HbA1c percent row (5.6,0.3); IFCC-derived percent values are alternative rounded representations, not independent calibration data. Assume source fasting plasma measurements can provisionally anchor target fasting serum scale, without asserting equivalence or eAG identity.

Completion scenario, not an evidence finding: BMI is independent of age and female; glucose has 0.06 mg/dL per year and 1.8 mg/dL per BMI SD components; HbA1c has 0.004 percentage points per year, 0.04 per BMI SD and 0.14 per unit shared glucose residual factor. Female has no direct effect. All coefficients/signs and independence assumptions are unestimated; E0 identifies none of the requested projections.

BMI uses a scaled beta distribution supported on [16,48] kg/m^2; residual factors use symmetric triangular laws with mean zero and variance one, support [-sqrt(6),sqrt(6)]. These convenient finite technical supports are not clinical population cutoffs or evidence-based tail laws.

For an analytical source-context check only, take source age independent of BMI, residual factors and female, with mean 55.5 and SD 9.9; a continuous uniform law 55.5 +/- sqrt(3)*9.9 demonstrates existence. Female has probability 0.597. This hypothetical source law is not a reconstructed Lifelines dataset, is not executed, and does not set target quotas. The same conditional continuous-variable equations are evaluated under these source moments.

Reported marginal SDs describe individual dispersion; estimator uncertainty is unreported and is not inferred from n or a confidence score. Parameters are fixed scenario inputs. Seeds describe residual/age sampling only, not estimate, structural or transport uncertainty. All Jansen representations share one cohort; NGSP is unit guidance.

No source-population replay is allocated. A generated target table cannot estimate a source-population discrepancy; all such comparisons are unavailable. Analytical checks establish the model equations only.
Identifiers are artificial sequential labels after row permutation and carry no subject linkage.

design.derivation: Task row count, eligibility and exact quotas; uniform within-band ages are an explicit completion assumption.

source_reference.derivation: Source-context centering/variance only. Female probability is retained as context and never used by target generator.

bmi.derivation: Beta shape follows mean and variance on assumed [16,48]; independent of age/female.

glucose.derivation: 91.8=18*5.1 and 9=18*0.5. Residual SD=sqrt(9^2-(0.06*9.9)^2-1.8^2). Age and BMI loadings are assumptions.

hba1c.derivation: Use published percent row once. Residual SD=sqrt(0.3^2-(0.004*9.9)^2-0.04^2-0.14^2). All non-marginal loadings are assumptions.

residual_law.derivation: Symmetric triangular factor support is +/-sqrt(6*variance); variance=1 fixes factor scale.

output.derivation: Contract order and fictional identifier prefix; no individual data inputs.
